details.description: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct is a 1.5-billion-parameter (1.54B total, 1.31B non-embedding) instruction-tuned chat model from Alibaba's Qwen team, released September 2024, one of the smallest general-purpose models in the Qwen2.5 lineup (only the 0.5B-Instruct model is smaller). It is licensed under Apache 2.0 and, per Qwen's model card, supports a 32,768-token context window. Qwen states the 2.5 generation adds more knowledge and improved coding, math, structured-data understanding, and JSON output generation over Qwen2.
advantages: Scores 73.2 on GSM8K and 55.2 on MATH, per Qwen's published Qwen2.5 evaluation results.
Scores 61.6 on HumanEval and 63.2 on MBPP for code generation, per Qwen's evaluation results.
Qwen's model card states it supports over 29 languages, including Chinese, English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Italian, Russian, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Thai and Arabic.
disadvantages: One of the smallest chat models in the Qwen2.5 family (only the 0.5B-Instruct model is smaller); scores lower than larger Qwen2.5 siblings on knowledge and reasoning benchmarks such as MMLU-Pro (32.4) and GPQA (29.8), per Qwen's evaluation results.
use_cases: Lightweight code generation and code understanding
Structured data understanding and JSON output generation

sources.title: Qwen2.5-LLM: Extending the boundary of LLMs

notes: Catalog's 32,768-token context length matches Qwen's model-card spec and Fireworks AI's listed context length for this deployment. Qwen's model card additionally states a max generation length of 8,192 tokens, which conflicts with catalog's max_output_tokens (32,768); the catalog value is kept and the maker's generation cap is not restated in the description. Corrected: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct is not the smallest chat model in the Qwen2.5 lineup — Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct is smaller and is benchmarked alongside it on Qwen's Qwen2.5-LLM blog. Only examples of the 29+ supported languages are named on Qwen's card (not an exhaustive list), so languages is left empty and the count is in the description instead.
